solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Eating colleague's tea somehow following predicament with maiden

indicators.note: following places the rearranged tea after the predicament and maiden

parts.note: a mess is a predicament or awkward fix
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of tea are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Somebody's tea has gone wrong because of an awkward situation involving a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The word after 'tea' signals its anagram, ATE, and 'following' sets that after the predicament and maiden. 'Eating colleague' is the definition, not a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A messmate is someone you share meals with in a mess, such as on a ship or in the forces.

clue.text: Stoke use biography to exhibit footballer

indicators.note: to exhibit means the words on show contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A biography from Stoke is used to put a football player on display.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'Stoke' through 'use' into 'biography'. Stoke is an English town with a football club, which makes 'Stoke' look like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Eusebio was the great Portuguese striker of the 1960s, star of Benfica and the 1966 World Cup.

clue.text: Wake up and photograph Oscar in costume

parts.note: a snap is a casual photograph

indicators.note: in places the Oscar letter inside the word for costume

parts.note: an outfit is a costume or set of clothes
O is Oscar in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone is told to take a picture of an Oscar statuette dressed up in fancy dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oscar' looks like the film award but is just the letter O, which 'in' puts inside OUTFIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap out of it is an idiom for shaking off a daze or mood, as if waking up.

clue.text: You said it finally looked correct!

parts.note: amen is said to agree heartily, like saying you said it

indicators.note: finally picks the end letter of the word looked

explanation.surface: An exclamation of agreement: at last it looked right!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one cheerful remark, but 'correct' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend something is to correct it, as with a text or law; both are verbs.

clue.text: Close to grave and terrible danger — get ready!

indicators.note: close to means the very end of the word grave, its last letter
terrible signals the letters of danger are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A warning that a grave and awful danger is near, so get ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' looks like 'near' but takes the end of 'grave'; 'terrible' turns DANGER into NGARDE.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call to take a defensive stance, telling an opponent to prepare.

clue.text: Musician bungling an exam

indicators.note: bungling suggests the letters of an exam are messed up into a different order

explanation.surface: A music student makes a mess of an examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Axeman is slang for a guitarist, the guitar being called an axe.

clue.text: Broadcast good music regularly on sailor's unseen instrument

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of music, the second and fourth

parts.note: a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor's music, played regularly on the radio, comes from an invisible instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes UI from mUsIc.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing air guitar means miming guitar playing with no instrument at all, so it cannot be seen.

clue.text: Big bird's bone uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters, the covering, are stripped off

parts.note: the femur is the thigh bone

explanation.surface: A large bird's bone has been dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncovered' looks like 'dug up' but removes the first and last letters of FEMUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird, second in size only to the ostrich.

clue.text: Island opposed to another being docked

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: docked means the tail is cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: another island here is Guam, in the western Pacific

explanation.surface: One island is set against another island that a ship has docked at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another island, GUAM, and 'being docked' cuts its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation of Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: Seeking activity in clubs, Iron Man maybe involved in accident

indicators.note: involved in places the clubs and avenger letters inside the word for accident

parts.note: a shunt is British slang for a minor car crash
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
Iron Man is one of Marvel's Avengers, so an example of an avenger

explanation.surface: Iron Man ends up in a crash while out among the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' splits the accident word after its first letter. A shunt is a British term for a car collision, and Iron Man is a Marvel Avenger.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger hunt is a party game where teams go looking for a list of items.

clue.text: A way out of the country?

parts.note: in Britain minor roads are lettered B, so this way is one of those

explanation.surface: Someone asks about a route for leaving the country.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, B roads are minor numbered roads, below the main A roads.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abroad means being overseas, in a foreign land beyond one's own borders.

clue.text: Fibre shown by witch wearing make-up

indicators.note: wearing means the witch has the make-up around her, so it goes inside

parts.note: rouge is red make-up for the cheeks
a hag is an ugly old witch

explanation.surface: A witch in make-up shows off her fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fibre' looks like the witch's moral fibre, but it is the definition, of the dietary kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughage is dietary fibre, the indigestible part of plant foods.

clue.text: Tough hours on a road with a slow-moving group?

parts.note: snails are a by-word for slowness; the query marks this as an example

explanation.surface: A tough slog of hours on the road behind a slow convoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard as nails is an idiom for someone very tough and unfeeling.

clue.text: Stronghold surrounding ancient city is beneficial

indicators.note: surrounding means the stronghold goes round the city

parts.note: a fort is a fortified stronghold
Thebes was an ancient city of Egypt and also of Greece

explanation.surface: A fortress built around an old city is a good thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts the city inside the stronghold before its final letter; 'is' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done for the best is meant to bring good results, though it may not seem so.

clue.text: Run a piece about hedonist

indicators.note: about here means the letters of run a piece are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to publish an article about a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run a piece' sounds like newspaper talk, and 'about' looks like 'on the subject of', but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicurean is someone devoted to pleasure, especially fine food and wine, after Epicurus.

clue.text: Travel around capital, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is as heard, giving one with the same sound

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Reports of travelling around the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to wander about with no fixed route.

clue.text: Composer turned back by force

indicators.note: turned means the word for back is flipped end to end

parts.note: fro means back, as in to and fro
F is the physics symbol for force

explanation.surface: A composer is driven back by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' looks like one phrase, but 'turned' reverses 'back', FRO, giving ORF.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Orff was the German composer of Carmina Burana.

clue.text: City understanding what the mob might hear?

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a big city in Brazil
tact is understanding and sensitivity towards others

explanation.surface: A city's understanding of what a crowd might listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riot Act was an old British law read aloud to order an unruly crowd to break up.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a crowd the riot act was to order it to break up, so a rioting mob hears it.

clue.text: Craft that gets people talking?

parts.note: craft can mean a ship that breaks up ice, and also a party game that breaks the social ice

explanation.surface: Some skill or knack that starts conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' reads as a skill but is a vessel; the ship clears ice, and the answer's other sense starts chat among strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: An icebreaker is both a ship for clearing ice and an activity that eases tension among strangers.

clue.text: Withdraw demand about heartless teacher

indicators.note: about means the word for demand goes round the remaining letters

parts.note: to exact is to demand payment

indicators.note: heartless means the middle of teacher is taken out, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Pull out because of demands about a teacher with no heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' keeps only the first and last letters of teacher, and 'about' wraps the demand word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw out or remove something, as a tooth is withdrawn.

clue.text: Perhaps glasses of whiskey are drunk following verbal agreement

indicators.note: following puts the whiskey and drunk letters after the spoken agreement
verbal means spoken, so the word for agreement is as heard

parts.note: aye is a yes, a sign of agreement
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: drunk means the letters of are are scrambled

explanation.surface: Glasses of whiskey get drunk once a deal is struck by word of mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps glasses' is the definition, not drinking vessels; 'drunk' scrambles are, after the whiskey letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses are one kind of eyewear, the general term for things worn on the eyes; hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: 1940s fashion spot admits us too on reflection

indicators.note: admits means the word for spot lets the other letters inside

parts.note: a zit is slang for a pimple or spot

indicators.note: on reflection means the words us too are seen as in a mirror, back to front

explanation.surface: Someone admits, thinking it over, that we too were spotted in a 1940s style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns us too around, giving OOTSU, and 'admits' puts that inside the spot word.
explanation.definitionFit: The zoot suit, with baggy trousers and a long jacket, was a style popular in the 1940s.

clue.text: Bachelor really put out firework

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in degrees
to anger someone is to put them out badly, a stronger form of annoy

explanation.surface: A single man is very upset about a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is a firework that goes off with a loud bang.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is a small firework that explodes loudly, common around Bonfire Night.

clue.text: British Prime Minister set up censor

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the name is turned to read upwards

parts.note: Sir Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A British prime minister has arranged censorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses PEEL in a down entry, giving LEEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleep is to censor rude words on air by covering them with a beep.

clue.text: Together nevertheless

definitions.meaning: ... also means even so or however

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means simultaneously, and as a sentence adverb it means however or even so.

clue.text: Cat's regular check over

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the letters are flipped to read the other way

parts.note: the MOT is the yearly roadworthiness test for cars in Britain

explanation.surface: A cat has its regular check-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's annual compulsory vehicle test; 'over' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tom is a male cat, short for tomcat.

clue.text: Mates playing new viola part?

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of mates are set to work in another order

explanation.surface: Friends play a fresh viola part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viola' looks like the string instrument, but it is the flower, hence the query.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the male pollen-bearing part of a flower, and the viola is a flower.

clue.text: Records effort to make artwork

parts.note: tapes are recordings, so records
a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: A recorded attempt at making a piece of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapestry is a woven textile art piece with a picture worked into it.
